# Capwise rate flux, the selected uniform kernel, and boundary incidences

This gives the rate-resolved version of `candidate 4dd22db8fd75566e`, using `candidate d3b1d852e0e3ae4b`. It retains the actual cap selections, allocated sections, and source labels. There is a positive capwise uniform-rate kernel when the section defect vanishes. A supporting section can instead have an atom at a positive rate, and a generic nonparallel cap can split a defect lying on its limiting boundary. Both distinctions have exact actual triangle calibrations below.

## 1. Actual joint cap records and three rate-resolved defects

Use the fixed finite-base, positive-body, finite-plane contact-row setting of the two dependencies. In particular K_z^j converge to positive K_z, L_j converge uniformly to a nonnegative finite-PL L positive in each fiber interior, source marks have uniform own balls and positive parameter values, and

    nu_ij=(sigma_ij/L_ij)rho_ij,
    sum_i nu_ij=dm_j/(M_j L_j),
    grad_X log L_j dm_j=M_j sum_i c_ij nu_ij,
    c_ij -> c_i, M_j -> M.

The inverse masses and surface logarithm masses are bounded, the bulk logarithms are uniformly integrable, and

    ell_j=(-log L_j)_+,
    r_j=lambda_j ell_j,  lambda_j ->0,
    0<=r_j<=R_*.

The last bound follows from the actual exponential-floor theorem in its separator setting; for a geometric calibration it may simply be checked directly. No reciprocal uniform integrability is assumed.

Retain one converging actual cap record

    H_j={a_j.z+u_j.X>=t_j} -> H={a.z+u.X>=t},
    |u_j|>=u_min>0,

with its SAME body selector s_j and allocated coarea measure Lambda_j. Proper sections are fully counted; at inside support body+section densities equal one; at outside support they coincide. A trace-preserving bounded record map is allowed only as in the audited cap compactification. It does not change any of these measures.

After a common subsequence define

    s_j ell_j eta_j delta_(r_j)
        -> s ell eta delta_0 + ahat_H,
    1_(H_j) nu_ij delta_(r_j)
        -> (nu_i^0 restricted to H) delta_0 + zetahat_i^H,
    ell_j Lambda_j delta_(r_j)
        -> ell Lambda delta_0 + shat_H.                (1)

Here ell=(-log L)_+, eta is the actual limiting normal-bundle surface measure, and nu_i^0 is the ordinary limiting labeled inverse measure. All three residuals are positive and lie over {L=0}. Moreover

    0<=ahat_H<=bhat,  0<=zetahat_i^H<=zetahat_i.       (2)

The section-log mass bound and ordinary section-log integrability are proved in the capwise unweighted dependency: allocated Gauss--Green controls its mass, and the limiting finite-PL zero set has no facet, so its ordinary section logarithm is integrable. Adding the bounded rate coordinate costs no extra estimate. Off {L=0}, logarithmic truncation identifies the ordinary parts at rate zero. The limiting cap hyperplane is volume-null for the ordinary inverse measures, while its possible defect incidence is deliberately retained in zetahat_i^H.

The projection of shat_H that forgets the rate is the old unweighted section defect s_H. Hence s_H=0 implies shat_H=0; this follows from positivity, not from a rate argument.

## 2. The exact rate-weighted allocated Gauss--Green identity

For an integer m>=1 set F_j=ell_j r_j^m. Its weak derivative is

    grad_X F_j=-(m+1)r_j^m grad_X log L_j.

Indeed r_j^m=0 whenever L_j>=1, so the positive-part cutoff needs no additional indicator. For each fixed j the function is Lipschitz, including across finite-PL creases; no interface measure occurs in its first weak derivative.

For a C1 physical test phi, the actual all-status identity is

    int_boundary s_j phi F_j n d eta_j
      =int_(H_j) F_j grad_X phi dm_j
        -M_j(m+1) sum_i c_ij int_(H_j) phi r_j^m d nu_ij
        +u_j int phi F_j d Lambda_j.                    (3)

On a proper cap this is divergence on the actual cap body. The inside/outside allocation rules give the same formula at support, exactly as in the unweighted dependency. The bulk term tends to zero by bulk-log uniform integrability and r_j->0 locally off the zero set. The other terms pass by their joint compact limits in (1). Thus

    -int phi n r^m d ahat_H
       =M(m+1) sum_i c_i int phi r^m d zetahat_i^H
                         -u int phi r^m d shat_H.       (4)

For m=0 this is the already proved unweighted capwise defect identity. Polynomial linear combinations and uniform C1 approximation then give, for every C1 g on the common rate interval,

    -int phi n g(r) d ahat_H
      =M sum_i c_i int phi [g(r)+r g'(r)] d zetahat_i^H
                         -u int phi g(r) d shat_H.      (5)

Continuous physical tests follow by density. Formula (5) is a vector identity in physical position. It does not put a freely selected normal argument on the volume or section terms, and it does not split ahat_H into positive source-labeled surface measures.

For complementary caps use the complementary body selector and the SAME section allocation. At every rate,

    ahat_H+ahat_(H^c)=bhat,
    zetahat_i^H+zetahat_i^(H^c)=zetahat_i,
    shat_(H^c)=shat_H.                                  (6)

The complementary normal is -u, so summing (5) cancels the section term and recovers the full-body rate flux. This is also a direct check on its sign.

The proof can be integrated against a retained cap-record law, provided all measures are compactified JOINTLY with the record and the same rate. All assertions are then for almost every actual record or as integrated identities. No new finite sub-selection with different weights is made.

## 3. The capwise positive kernel when the section defect vanishes

Choose fixed fiber inball centers g_z. On the actual limiting boundary bundle put

    h(n,z,X)=n.(X-g_z)>=r_b>0.

On zetahat_i^H, the inherited contact equality A_i(z,X)=L(z,X)=0 gives

    c_i.(X-g_z)=-A_i(z,g_z),  A_i(z,g_z)>0.

Define the positive physical/rate measures

    B_H=pi_(w,r)*(h ahat_H),
    V_H=M sum_i A_i(z,g_z) zetahat_i^H.                 (7)

If shat_H=0, dot (4) with X-g_z. For every continuous physical phi and every m>=0,

    int phi r^m dV_H=(m+1)^(-1) int phi r^m dB_H.       (8)

Exactly the compact moment argument of the full-body theorem proves

    V_H(dw,ds)=int U_R(ds) B_H(dw,dR),                 (9)

where U_R is uniform on [0,R] for R>0 and U_0=delta_0. This is a kernel identity for the ACTUAL cap-restricted inverse defects and ACTUAL selected surface defects. Both are submeasures of their corresponding full-body measures.

There is also a precise signed formula when the section defect is present. Let

    C_H(dw,dr)=[u.(X-g_z)] shat_H(dw,dr).

The radial form of (4) is

    int phi r^m dB_H=(m+1) int phi r^m dV_H
                                      +int phi r^m dC_H.

Moment uniqueness therefore gives V_H=K(B_H-C_H), with K the same uniform-rate kernel, understood for signed finite measures. No positivity of B_H-C_H is asserted in general. The genuinely positive conclusion (9) uses shat_H=0.

## 4. Geometric criterion for zero section defect

The independently proved `candidate 53c44db9ae559bfe` applies fiberwise to the same compact finite affine presentation. It establishes

    s_H nonzero at base z
       => {u.X=t-a.z} is the zero plane of some A_r(z,.),
          u is parallel to its nonzero continuous gradient c_r,
          K_z intersect {u.X=t-a.z} is wholly zero for L,
          and that exposed face has dimension at most d-2. (10)

In particular every limiting PROPER fiber section has zero defect. If u is not parallel to any of the finitely many nonzero continuous gradients of the limiting affine presentation, all s_H and hence shat_H vanish. The finite presentation, not just uniform convergence of arbitrary concave functions, is essential for this normal classification.

Under this generic nonparallel hypothesis, (9) is a positive capwise kernel without any assumption that the cap avoids the zero set. Avoiding the zero set is a separate issue for literal closed-cap restriction.

## 5. Literal restrictions, and the exact rate-mixture constraint at incidence

If the limiting cap boundary has zero bhat mass (equivalently zero B physical marginal there), it also has zero total inverse defect mass. This equivalence follows from the full radial identity: B and V have the same physical marginal, and both radial/source-plane weights are bounded above and below by positive constants. Stable strict cap signs then give

    ahat_H=1_H bhat,
    zetahat_i^H=1_H zetahat_i.                           (11)

Thus B_H=1_H B and V_H=1_H V. In this incidence-null situation (9) is the literal restriction of the full kernel to H. Since the kernel preserves the physical position, restriction commutes with it. Closed/open cap conventions agree for these defect measures.

Without incidence-nullness one must retain (7), even if u is generic nonparallel. There is nevertheless an exact constraint on the fractional selection. Write w_H=dB_H/dB, so 0<=w_H<=1. Disintegrate B over its physical marginal, with conditional rate measures B_w. When shat_H=0, the positive-rate cap-selected inverse density at physical w is

    s -> int_(R>=s) w_H(w,R) B_w(dR)/R,                (12)

whereas the full inverse density is int_(R>=s) B_w(dR)/R. Their ratio is the actual aggregate radially weighted inverse cap fraction whenever the denominator is positive. This is a weighted tail average, not an arbitrary independent allocation at each rate.

In particular, if B_w is concentrated at a single positive rate R, the inverse cap fraction is the SAME constant w_H(w,R) for almost every s in (0,R). This is a new restriction on the joint rate/cap incidence data. It concerns the source-plane weighted aggregate in (7); it does not identify individual source rows or remove their weights. At rate zero one retains the separate possible atomic part of the kernel.

## 6. Actual supporting sections may have a positive-rate atom

Use the exact triangle family from Section 5 of `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`:

    a=1/m, eta=exp(-gamma m),
    K_m={x,y>=0:a<=t=x+y<=1},
    L_m=c_m(t-a+eta), c_m->c=exp(1/2),
    lambda_m=R/(gamma m).

It has one actual affine contact row, uniform source cores and floors, and

    bhat=sqrt(2) gamma delta_(n0,0,R),
    zetahat=(2gamma/c) delta_0(dw) U_R(ds),
    n0=-(1,1)/sqrt(2), M=1/2, c_source=c(1,1).        (13)

Take the inside supporting cap H_m={t>=a}, with body allocation zero on the bottom facet and section allocation one. The bottom coarea is a, and its negative logarithm is gamma m-log c_m. Therefore

    ahat_H=0,
    zetahat^H=zetahat,
    shat_H=gamma delta_(0,R),  u=(1,1).               (14)

This is an ATOM at a positive section rate R. For any C1 g,

    int_[0,R] [g(s)+s g'(s)] ds/R=g(R),

so the two terms on the right of (5) cancel exactly. Thus a positive-rate section atom is not only allowed but is precisely what the capwise rate identity requires here. Tangential section Gauss--Green cannot imply a universal uniform-rate law for these collapsing sections.

The same phenomenon occurs with strictly PROPER prelimit caps H_m={t>=a+eta^2}. Their lower excluded collar has inverse mass bounded by a log(1+eta)+O(eta^2), hence tends to zero. Their body defect is zero and their section coarea a+eta^2, logarithm gamma m-log c_m-log(1+eta), and rate again yield exactly (14). Thus proper prelimit status does not repair the failed section-kernel assertion.

For the complementary cap, ahat_(H^c)=bhat, zetahat^(H^c)=0, and its normal is -(1,1); the same section atom makes (5) true. At the limiting vertex, literal closed H and H^c both contain the entire zero point, but the actual volume selections in (14) are different. This is why prelimit incidences must be retained.

## 7. Generic nonparallel cuts still need fractional boundary selections

On the SAME triangle sequence choose the fixed proper cap H={x-y>=0}. Its normal (1,-1) is not parallel to the only continuous parameter gradient (1,1). Symmetry splits every t-slice and the bottom edge in half, with the actual rate depending only on t. Consequently

    ahat_H=bhat/2,
    zetahat^H=zetahat/2,
    shat_H=0.                                         (15)

The last assertion also follows from (10), or from the elementary one-dimensional logarithmic integral on x=y. Thus (9) holds exactly with B_H=B/2 and V_H=V/2.

However the limiting closed halfspace H contains the zero vertex, so the literal restriction 1_H bhat is ALL of bhat and 1_H zetahat is ALL of zetahat. Equation (15) is an exact counterexample to asserting (11) merely from nonparallelity or vanishing section defect. It illustrates the valid constant-in-rate fractional selection in Section 5 instead.

No cap in these two calibrations is asserted to be part of a globally deepest physical stationary menu. They are actual geometric/contact-row sequences satisfying the flux and compactness hypotheses, which is the precise scope needed to test the rate-kernel and incidence assertions. There is no defect exclusion or Gamma conclusion.

The checker `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_capwise_rate_flux_and_incidence_slab_recovery.py` verifies the derivative/primitive identities, complementary signs, capwise moment factors, proper-collar estimate, and actual triangle symmetry allocations. The general measure limits are proved in the preceding sections.
